# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XXV. Obed Insists on Puffed Sleeves

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

OBED was experiencing a disagreeable ten minutes. During the twilight of a chilly, gray December evening, he had entered the kitchen and sat down near the woodbox corner to remove his heavy boots, unaware that Nell and a group of her schoolmates were practicing “The Fairy Queen” inside the sitting room. Shortly afterward, they came trooping through the hall and into the kitchen, laughing and chatting merrily. Shrinking bashfully back into the shadows behind the woodbox while holding a boot in one hand and a bootjack in the other, Obed was not seen by them, and he shyly observed them for the aforementioned ten minutes while they put on caps and jackets and spoke about the dialogue and the concert. Nell stood in their midst, as bright eyed and animated as the rest; however, Obed all at once realized that there was something about her that differed from her companions. And what troubled Obed was that this distinction struck him as a thing that ought not to be present. Nell possessed a brighter face, alongside larger, starrier eyes, and finer features than the others; even shy, unobservant Obed had come to notice these aspects; yet the distinction that unsettled him was not found in any of these details. In what, then, did it lie?
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0000 }

Obed remained troubled by this inquiry well after the young women had departed, hand in hand, along the lengthy, deeply frozen path and Nell had retreated to her reading. He was unable to bring it up to Thirza, who, he sensed, would certainly turn up her nose in disdain and observe that the sole distinction she perceived between Nell and the rest of the girls was that the others occasionally held their peace whereas Nell never ceased talking. Such an answer, Obed realized, would offer little assistance.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0001 }

That night, he turned to his pipe to assist him in figuring it out, which greatly disgusted Thirza. Obed reached an answer to his dilemma following two hours of smoking and intense thought. The other girls did not dress the way Nell did!
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0002 }

As Obed pondered the issue further, his certainty grew that Nell had failed to dress like her peers at any point following her arrival at Grey Shutters. Thirza ensured her wardrobe consisted of simple, somber garments, which were entirely crafted from a single, unchanging design. Obed barely possessed an awareness that clothes followed shifting trends, yet he possessed complete certainty that the sleeves on Nell’s dresses bore no resemblance to those worn by her peers. His memory returned to the group of young girls who had gathered near her that night, each bright in a bodice of crimson, navy, rose, or ivory, causing him to question the reasons behind Thirza’s insistence on keeping her in such simple and subdued attire at all times.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0003 }

Naturally, everything had to be fine. Thirza was the authority, and Thirza was raising her. It was likely that this acted to fulfill a clever, incomprehensible purpose. Nevertheless, allowing the young girl a single attractive gown—a garment resembling the ones Isolde Pembroke continually dressed in—certainly could cause no injury. Obed resolved to present her with one; undoubtedly nobody could oppose that as an unjustified interference on his part. Christmas lay merely two weeks away. An attractive, freshly made dress would serve as the ideal gift. Obed, exhaling a pleased sigh, stowed his pipe and retired to sleep, as Thirza flung open every door and ventilated the dwelling.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0004 }

On the immediately following evening, Obed headed to Delford so that he might purchase the garment, resolved to undergo the worst of it and be finished. He was convinced that this would prove to be a far from minor trial. While Obed was capable of purchasing certain items and showing that he was quite a skilled negotiator, he was aware that he would be completely defenseless against storekeepers regarding the purchase of a young woman's dress.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0005 }

Upon extensive deliberation, Obed decided he would head to Samuel Lawson’s shop rather than William Blair’s. Indeed, attending William Blair’s had constantly been the habit of the Abernethys; following this custom was nearly a point of morality for the family, akin to going to the Presbyterian church and casting a Conservative vote. Nevertheless, the two daughters of William Blair often served patrons in that shop, and Obed possessed a complete terror of them. Whenever he was aware of the precise item he desired and was able to indicate it, he managed to conduct business with them; yet regarding a situation like this one, which demanded explaining and advice, Obed believed he needed to guarantee a male presence on the other side of the counter. Consequently, he intended to head to Lawson’s, where either Samuel or his son would attend to his needs.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0006 }

Alas! Samuel had hired a female clerk as well during the latest growth of his trade, a detail Obed failed to realize; this woman was his wife’s niece and truly a very bold young lady, possessing a massive, hanging pompadour, large, roving brown eyes, and an exceptionally broad and dazing smile. Attired with extreme elegance, she wore a number of bangle bracelets that shone, clattered, and chimed whenever her hands moved. Discovering her in that place at all filled Obed with embarrassment; moreover, those very bangles entirely destroyed his composure all at once.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0007 }

With a quick, pleasant manner, Miss Lucilla Harris drummed her fingers on the counter and asked, “How may I assist you tonight, Mr. Abernethy?”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0008 }

“Is there any—any—any—well, let’s say garden rakes available?” Obed stammered.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0009 }

Miss Harris appeared rather astonished, which was understandable, when a man asked about garden rakes during mid-December.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0010 }

“I think there are one or two remaining,” she remarked, “however they are up in the lumber room. I will fetch them.” While she was away, Obed gathered his dispersed faculties to try once more.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0011 }

As Miss Harris came back carrying the rake and brightly asked: “Anything else tonight, Mr. Abernethy?” Obed plucked up his bravery and answered: “Well now, since you suggest it, I might as well—take—that is—look at—buy some—some hayseed.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0012 }

Miss Harris had been told that Obed Abernethy was considered strange. She now decided that he was completely insane.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0013 }

“In the spring is the only time we stock hayseed,” she haughtily clarified. “Right now, we don’t have any in stock.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0014 }

“Oh, certainly—certainly—just as you say,” stuttered miserable Obed, grabbing the rake and heading toward the doorway. Upon reaching the threshold, he remembered he had failed to pay for the item and turned around in distress. As Miss Harris counted out his change, he summoned his strength for one last, desperate effort.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0015 }

“Well now—provided it is not excessively inconvenient—I may just as well—namely—I would enjoy viewing—viewing—a portion of sugar.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0016 }

“White or brown?” Miss Harris inquired with patience.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0017 }

“Oh—well now—brown,” Obed said weakly.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0018 }

“A barrel of it is over there,” Miss Harris said, her bangles shaking toward the spot. “We don’t have any other kind.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0019 }

“I will—I will buy twenty pounds of it,” stated Obed, who had drops of sweat forming upon his forehead.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0020 }

By the time Obed reached the midpoint of his journey back, he had finally regained his composure. Although the ordeal was harrowing, he believed he deserved it for the disloyal act of visiting an unfamiliar shop. Upon arriving at his house, he concealed the rake inside the tool house, whereas the sugar was brought indoors by him to Thirza.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0021 }

“Brown sugar!” Thirza cried out. “What on earth made you purchase such a large amount? You are aware that I only ever utilize it when making porridge for the hired man or for black fruit cake. Tobias has departed, and my cake was baked a long time back. Furthermore, this sugar is inferior—it is dark and coarse—the sort of sugar William Blair fails to stock ordinarily.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0022 }

“I—I believed it could prove useful at some point,” Obed stated, successfully slipping away.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0023 }

Upon reflecting on the issue, Obed concluded that managing the circumstances called for a woman's touch. Thirza could not be considered, as Obed was convinced she would immediately discourage his plan. That left solely Mrs. Sowerby, since Obed lacked the courage to seek counsel from any other female inhabitant of Brierley. Consequently, he visited Mrs. Sowerby, and the kind woman immediately relieved the troubled man of the responsibility.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0024 }

“Select a gown for you to bestow upon Nell? Of course I shall. My journey to Delford takes place tomorrow, when I shall manage it. Do you have a specific preference? You do not? In that case, I will simply rely upon my own taste. It is my opinion that a lovely, deep brown would be ideal for Nell, and William Blair currently stocks some newly arrived gloria that is quite charming. Would it suit you if I also fashioned the garment for her, considering that were Thirza to craft it, Nell might learn of it prematurely and ruin the unexpected gift? Very well, I shall undertake it. Truly, it is no inconvenience whatsoever. Dressmaking pleases me. The measurements of my niece, Jenny Pettigrew, will serve for its construction, because her form and Nell’s are identical in every respect.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0025 }

“Well now, I am very thankful,” Obed said, “and—and—I do not know—but I would want—I believe they craft sleeves in a way that is distinct today from how they used to do it. If it would not be overstepping I—I would want them crafted in the current fashion.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0026 }

“Puffs? Naturally. Not another bit of concern is needed on your part, Obed. The most recent style will be used when I craft it,” Mrs. Sowerby stated. Once Obed had departed, she remarked to herself:
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0027 }

“Viewing that unfortunate child in proper clothing for a change will bring true pleasure. The manner in which Thirza garments her is entirely absurd, no two ways about it, and I have longed to inform her directly as much on twelve separate occasions. I kept silent, however, because I recognize that Thirza desires no counsel and imagines she possesses greater knowledge regarding child-rearing than I do, despite her status as an old maid. Yet that is consistently how it goes. People who have raised children realize that not a single rigid technique exists anywhere to fit every individual child. Conversely, those who have never raised any believe the whole process is as straightforward and simple as Rule of Three—merely arrange your three factors in such a manner, and the total will prove accurate. However, living beings fail to fall beneath the category of mathematics, and that represents the exact area where Thirza Abernethy errs. It seems to me she is attempting to foster a humble disposition in Nell through her choice of attire; nevertheless, such a method is far more apt to breed bitterness and dissatisfaction. I feel certain the young girl has to perceive the contrast separating her garments from those worn by the remaining girls. Yet to imagine Obed observing it! That fellow is coming to life following a period of slumber lasting more than sixty years.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0028 }

Throughout the entire next two weeks, Thirza was aware that Obed was troubled by something, though its exact nature remained a mystery to her until Christmas Eve, the day Mrs. Sowerby delivered the new dress. Thirza conducted herself reasonably well for the most part, even if she probably doubted the tactful reason Mrs. Sowerby offered, claiming she had crafted the dress herself since Obed feared Nell might discover it prematurely were Thirza to sew it.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0029 }

“So this is the thing that Obed has appeared so secret about and chuckled to himself over for two weeks, isn't it?” she remarked somewhat coldly yet patiently. “I was aware he was engaged in some silly business. Well, I have to state I do not believe Nell required further dresses. I sewed her three fine, warm, practical ones this autumn, and whatever else is pure wastefulness. The fabric in those sleeves by itself is sufficient to construct a waist, I assert it is. You will simply indulge Nell’s pride, Obed, and she is already as proud as a peacock. Well, I trust she will finally be pleased, because I am aware she has been longing for those foolish sleeves from the time they arrived, even though she didn't utter a thing following the initial time. The gathers have been growing larger and more absurd continuously; currently they are as large as balloons. During the coming year, anyone who wears them will be forced to pass through a doorway side-on.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0030 }

Christmas day arrived upon a lovely pale landscape. December had proved exceptionally gentle, leading folk to anticipate a snowless holiday; yet a gentle overnight snowfall sufficed to alter the appearance of Brierley. Nell peered through her icy gable window, her eyes filled with joy. Feathery marvels now filled the Whispering Wood’s firs; a pearly border traced the birches and wild cherry-trees; the tilled ground lay as expanses of indented snow; while a splendid, sharp freshness filled the air. Nell hurried down the stairs, her song echoing throughout Grey Shutters.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0031 }

“Merry Christmas, Thirza! Merry Christmas, Obed! Is this not a wonderful Christmas? I am delighted that it is white. No other sort of Christmas feels authentic, does it? Green Christmases are not to my liking. Green is not what they are—they are merely unpleasant washed-out browns and grays. For what reason do people label them green? Why—why—Obed, does that belong to me? Oh, Obed!”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0032 }

In an embarrassed manner, Obed had removed the garment from its paper wrapping, displaying it while shooting an apologetic look toward Thirza; she pretended to be disdainfully topping up the teapot, yet she still observed what was happening from the edge of her vision with somewhat intrigued curiosity.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0033 }

Nell accepted the garment and examined it, silently filled with awe. Oh, it possessed such beauty—a charming, gentle brown gloria displaying the full sheen of silk; a skirt adorned with delicate frills and gathers; a bodice intricately pintucked in the utmost stylish manner, featuring a small ruffle of delicate lace around the collar. However, the sleeves—they represented the supreme feature! Extended elbow cuffs, with two gorgeous puffs positioned above them, separated by bands of gathering and bows crafted from brown-silk ribbon.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0034 }

“Nell, that is a gift for Christmas for you,” Obed stated timidly. “Why—why—Nell, is it not to your liking? Well now—well now.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0035 }

For moisture had unexpectedly brimmed in Nell’s eyes.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0036 }

“Enjoy it! Oh, Obed!” Nell placed the gown across a seat and joined her hands together. “Obed, it’s completely marvelous. Oh, I will never be able to express sufficient gratitude to you. Observe those sleeves! Oh, I feel as though this has to be a delightful dream.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0037 }

“Oh, come on, let’s eat breakfast,” Thirza chimed in. “I have to admit, Nell, that I feel the dress wasn't necessary for you; however, now that it has been bought for you by Obed, ensure it is well maintained. Mrs. Sowerby left a hair ribbon behind for you. To go with the dress, it is brown. Move along, take your seat.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0038 }

“I do not understand how I will manage to consume breakfast,” Nell stated ecstatically. “At a time of such great excitement, eating breakfast feels entirely ordinary. Looking at that gown provides me far greater pleasure. That puffy sleeves remain in style brings me immense joy. Should the trend have ended prior to my owning a dress featuring them, I felt I would remain perpetually heartbroken. You understand, I would have lacked complete contentment otherwise. Mrs. Sowerby showed such sweetness by bestowing the ribbon upon me as well. I sense a deep obligation to conduct myself as a truly well-behaved child. Moments such as these make me regret that I fail to be an exemplary young lady; consequently, I constantly determine to become one moving forward. Nevertheless, executing your intentions proves difficult whenever overwhelming allurements arise. Even so, I shall genuinely exert a heightened endeavor following this.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0039 }

As soon as the ordinary morning meal came to an end Isolde emerged, coming over the white log bridge down in the hollow, appearing as a bright small figure in her crimson ulster. Nell rushed down the incline to greet her.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0040 }

“I wish you a Merry Christmas, Isolde! Truly, this Christmas is marvelous. Something magnificent is here for me to display to you. The most beautiful dress has been presented to me by Obed, featuring incredible sleeves. Any finer ones were beyond my capability to picture.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0041 }

“I have another item to give you,” Isolde uttered, out of breath. “Look—this container. Aunt Lavinia shipped us a large crate filled with numerous items—and you are meant to have this. Though I wanted to deliver it yesterday evening, its arrival occurred after nightfall, and passing through the Whispering Wood after dark makes me feel quite uneasy these days.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0042 }

Peering inside after opening the box, Nell found a card initialised with the words “For the Nell-girl and Merry Christmas,” lying on top; beneath it rested a pair of kid slippers, remarkably delicate and small, which featured beaded toes, satin bows, and sparkling buckles.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0043 }

“Oh,” Nell uttered, “Isolde, this goes beyond reason. I have to be dreaming.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0044 }

“I deem it providential,” Isolde remarked. “Now there is no need for you to borrow the slippers belonging to Opal, which is fortunate, as they are two sizes overly large for your feet, and the sound of a shuffling fairy would be terrible. Flossie Tulk is sure to be pleased. Though remember, Tibby Tulk was accompanied home by Rob Duckett after the practice two nights ago. Have you ever known anything to match that?”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0045 }

A fever of excitement consumed every one of the Brierley scholars on that day, as it was necessary to decorate the hall and hold a final grand rehearsal.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0046 }

That night, the concert took place and turned into an undeniable triumph. Packed to capacity, the small hall hosted magnificent performances from everyone involved, yet Nell shone as the true luminary of the event, a fact so clear that even malice, embodied by Flossie Tulk, could not bring itself to dispute.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0047 }

“Oh, hasn’t it been a brilliant evening?” sighed Nell, when everything had concluded and she and Isolde were making their way home together beneath a dark, starry sky.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0048 }

“Things proceeded quite smoothly,” Isolde remarked in a matter-of-fact way. “It seems to me that our earnings reached fully ten dollars. Remember, Mr. Wace intends to forward a report about it to the newspapers in Port Marlow.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0049 }

“Oh, Isolde, are our names truly going to appear in print? Thinking about it gives me a thrill. Isolde, the solo you performed was completely elegant. Seeing it get encored made me feel even prouder than you were. To myself, I simply said, ‘It is my dear bosom friend who is so honored.’”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0050 }

“Truly, Nell, those pieces you recited were a huge success with the audience. The sorrowful one was absolutely marvelous.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0051 }

“Oh, I felt so anxious, Isolde. Whenever Mr. Wace shouted my name, I truly am unable to say how I ever managed to walk up on that stage. It seemed to me as though one million eyes were staring at me and penetrating through me, and during one terrible second I felt certain I would be unable to start whatsoever. After that, I remembered my beautiful puffed sleeves and found bravery. I realized that I had to be worthy of those sleeves, Isolde. Therefore I commenced, and my voice appeared to originate from a great distance. I simply felt similar to a parrot. It is a blessing from God that I rehearsed those recitations so many times up in the attic, or I would not have managed to finish. Was my groaning acceptable?”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0052 }

“Yes, truly, the way you groaned was lovely,” Isolde assured.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0053 }

“I noticed aged Mrs. Mott dabbing at her eyes as I took my seat. Thinking that I had moved someone’s heart was wonderful. Participating in a concert is so romantic, wouldn’t you say? Ah, this has truly been a most unforgettable event.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0054 }

“Didn’t the dialogue between the boys turn out splendidly?” asked Isolde. “Hugh Carrow performed wonderfully. Nell, I honestly believe you are terribly unkind to Hughie. Let me share something with you. Following the fairy dialogue, as you hurried away from the platform, a rose dropped from your hair. I noticed Hughie retrieve it and place it inside his jacket pocket. So there. Given how romantic you are, I feel certain this should delight you.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0055 }

“Whatever that individual does doesn't matter to me,” Nell remarked haughtily. “Isolde, I straightforwardly never spend a single thought regarding him.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0056 }

Having attended a concert for the first time in twenty years, Thirza and Obed sat near the hearth in the kitchen for a short time that evening, once Nell was asleep.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0057 }

“Well now, I reckon our Nell performed just as effectively as the rest,” Obed remarked with pride.
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0058 }

“Yes, she did,” Thirza conceded. “She’s a clever girl, Obed. And she looked truly lovely as well. I’ve been somewhat against this concert plan, but I guess it isn't actually damaging when all is said and done. In any case, I felt pride in Nell this evening, even if I won't be letting her know it.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0059 }

“Well now, I felt pride in her and I indeed expressed it to her ‘fore her ascent upstairs,” declared Obed. “We have to consider what assistance we can provide her one of these days, Thirza. It is my expectation that she will require something beyond Brierley school in time.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0060 }

“There’s time enough to think of that,” Thirza said. “In March she’s only thirteen. Although tonight it struck me she was becoming quite a big girl. That dress was made a mite too long by Mrs. Sowerby, and Nell looks so tall because of it. She is quick to learn and I guess sending her to Regent’s after a spell will be the best thing we can do for her. However, for a year or two yet nothing need be said about that.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0061 }

“Well now, giving it some thought now and then won’t cause any trouble,” Obed said. “Matters of that sort only improve with a great deal of consideration.”
{: #nw-v01-c25-p0062 }
